summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, recent coronary stent placement, and chronic osteoarthritis was admitted for acute right knee pain and subjective fevers. Initial concerns included infection or gout flare, but evaluation showed no evidence of septic arthritis, pneumonia, or active gout. Knee X-ray revealed stable degenerative changes without fracture, and blood cultures were negative. Leukocytosis resolved spontaneously, attributed to a stress reaction. The pain was determined to be from osteoarthritis, and the patient received dialysis during admission. He was discharged home with optimized medications, discontinuation of allopurinol and gabapentin, and plans for outpatient orthopedic follow-up and cardiac rehabilitation.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
